properties.headline: Special Marine Warning issued November 21 at 6:39AM EST until November 21 at 7:45AM EST by NWS Miami FL
properties.description:
SMWMFL

The National Weather Service in Miami has issued a

* Special Marine Warning for...
Coastal waters from Chokoloskee to Bonita Beach FL out 20 NM...
Coastal waters from East Cape Sable to Chokoloskee FL out 20 NM...
Waters from Chokoloskee to Bonita Beach FL from 20 to 60 NM...

* Until 745 AM EST.

* At 639 AM EST, a strong thunderstorm was located near D Tower,
moving northeast at 30 knots.

HAZARD...Wind gusts to nearly 50 knots.

SOURCE...Radar.

IMPACT...Small craft could be damaged in briefly higher winds and
suddenly higher waves.

* Locations impacted include...
Chokoloskee, D Tower, Chevelier Bay, Cape Romano Aquatic Preserve,
Cape Romano, and Marco Island.
properties.instruction:
Move to safe harbor until hazardous weather passes.

Report severe weather to the Coast Guard or the National Weather
Service. You can also share your report with NWS Miami on Facebook
and Twitter.

properties.description:
SMWKEY

The National Weather Service in Key West has issued a

* Special Marine Warning for...
Gulf Waters from East Cape Sable to Chokoloskee 20 to 60 nm out and
beyond 5 fathoms...

* Until 700 AM EST.

* At 629 AM EST, a strong thunderstorm was located 9 nm southwest of
D Tower, moving northeast at 25 knots.

HAZARD...Wind gusts 34 knots or greater.

SOURCE...National Weather Service Meteorologist.

IMPACT...Expect wind gusts in excess of 34 knots, suddenly higher
waves, frequent lightning, and heavy downpours.

* The strong thunderstorm will remain over mainly open waters.
properties.instruction:
Prepare for wind gusts in excess of 34 knots, steep and fast-building
seas, frequent lightning, and blinding downpours. Stay low or go
below, and make sure all on board are wearing life jackets.

Intense and continuous lightning is occurring with this storm. Stay
low, or go below. Lower VHF antenna, outriggers, fishing rods, and
umbrellas.

properties.areaDesc: San Juan and Vicinity; Northeast; North Central; Northwest; Mayaguez and Vicinity
properties.headline: Rip Current Statement issued November 21 at 4:10AM AST until November 21 at 6:00PM AST by NWS San Juan PR
properties.description:
* WHAT...Life-threatening rip current.

* WHERE...From Rincon to Fajardo

* WHEN...Through this afternoon

* IMPACTS...Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water, where it becomes difficult to
return to safety.
properties.instruction:
There is a high risk of rip currents.

Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as groins, jetties
and piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

If you become caught in a rip current, yell for help. Remain
calm, do not exhaust yourself and stay afloat while waiting for
help. If you have to swim out of a rip current, swim parallel to
shore and back toward the beach when possible. Do not attempt to
swim directly against a rip current as you will tire quickly.

properties.headline: High Surf Advisory issued November 21 at 1:30AM EST until November 22 at 7:00AM EST by NWS Jacksonville FL
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Warning, significant coastal
flooding. For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 5
to 8. For the High Rip Current Risk, dangerous rip currents.

* WHERE...Coastal Flagler County.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Warning, until 7 AM EST Sunday.
For the High Rip Current Risk, through Sunday morning.

* IMPACTS...Numerous roads may be closed. Low lying property
including homes, businesses, and some critical infrastructure
will be inundated. Some shoreline erosion will occur.
Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and localized beach
erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water.
properties.instruction:
Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone property. If
travel is required, do not drive around barricades or through
water of unknown depth.

Inexperienced swimmers should remain out of the water due to
dangerous surf conditions.

Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

observations.

properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued November 20 at 8:44PM PST until November 25 at 3:00AM PST by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 7
to 10 feet with dangerous rip currents. High surf will likely
continue much of next week, peaking on Wednesday and Thursday.
For the Coastal Flood Advisory, moderate coastal flooding
expected. For the Coastal Flood Watch, significant coastal
flooding possible.

* WHERE...San Luis Obispo County Beaches, Santa Barbara County
Central Coast Beaches, Ventura County Beaches, Malibu Coast
and Los Angeles County Beaches.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 3 AM Monday to 3
AM PST Wednesday. For the Coastal Flood Watch, from late
Tuesday night through Thursday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...There is a moderate risk for damaging flooding of
sea water over some vulnerable low-lying coastal areas,
especially around the time of high tide, including over
beaches, roads, and structures. Significant beach erosion is
possible. There is an increased risk for ocean drowning. Rip
currents can pull swimmers and surfers out to sea. Large
breaking waves can cause injury, wash people off beaches and
rocks, and capsize small boats near shore.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Highest risk likely Wednesday and
Thursday with potential for significant impacts. Additional
products will likely be needed into Friday.
properties.instruction:
Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone property. Plan
for extra travel time as some roads may be closed.

Remain out of the water due to dangerous surf conditions, or stay
near occupied lifeguard towers. Rock jetties can be deadly in
such conditions, stay off the rocks.

properties.instruction:

properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued November 20 at 8:34PM PST until November 21 at 10:00AM PST by NWS Eureka CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, High astronomical tides
will cause minor flooding in low lying areas around Humboldt
Bay. Up to one half foot of saltwater inundation above ground
level is possible near shorelines and tidal waterways. For the
Coastal Flood Watch, High astronomical tides and large surf
may cause major flooding in low lying areas along the
Redwood/Mendocino Coast. Up to 2.5 to 3 feet of saltwater
inundation above ground level is possible in low lying areas
near shorelines and tidal waterways during the highest tides
if storm impacts such as strong southerly winds and large surf
arrive during high tide periods.

* WHERE...Northern Coastal Humboldt County, especially for areas
in and around Humboldt Bay.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 7 AM to 10 AM PST
Saturday with high tide at 8:31 AM on Saturday at the Humboldt
Bay North Spit tide gauge. For the Coastal Flood Watch, from
Sunday morning through Thursday afternoon. High tide is at
9:06 AM on Sunday, 9:44 AM on Monday, 10:25 AM on Tuesday,
11:09 AM on Wednesday, 11:56 AM on Thursday, 12:48 AM on
Friday at the Humboldt Bay North Spit tide gauge. Saltwater
inundation will be possible 1 to 2 hours before and after high
tide.

* IMPACTS...Several coastal roads may be closed. Low lying
property and some critical infrastructure will be inundated.
Some shoreline erosion may occur.
properties.instruction:
A Coastal Flood Watch means that flooding is possible but not
imminent. Coastal residents in the watch area should begin
preparations for rising water and take appropriate action to
protect life and property.

Feet Above Ground is locally defined as feet above the Highest
Astronomical Tide or HAT.

properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Deland affecting Volusia and Lake Counties.

.Heavy rainfall has maintained a steady climb into Moderate Flood
Stage on the St Johns River at Deland, with river levels forecast to
continue climbing through next week. The river is anticipated to
reach Major Flood Stage this weekend, with additional rises
thereafter.

For the St. Johns River...including Deland...Major flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Moderate flooding is occurring and major flooding is
forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Deland.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 5.3 feet, Major flooding occurs to many structures and
marinas along the river and in the Hontoon Island area.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 8:30 PM EST Friday the stage was 5.0 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 3.5 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 8:30 PM EST Friday was 5.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to 6.0 feet early next
week. Additional rises are possible thereafter.
- Flood stage is 4.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued Saturday afternoon at noon EST.

properties.areaDesc: Brevard, FL; Volusia, FL
properties.headline: Flood Warning issued November 20 at 6:10PM EST until November 21 at 8:00AM EST by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
* WHAT...Urban and small stream flooding caused by excessive rainfall
is occurring.

* WHERE...Northern Brevard County in east central Florida...
Eastern Volusia County in east central Florida...

* WHEN...Until 800 AM EST Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is imminent or occurring. Some roads are
impassable or closed.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 607 PM EST, emergency management reported flooding in the
warned area. While heavy rain has ended, flooding will be slow to
recede tonight.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Daytona Beach, Port Orange, Titusville, Ormond Beach, Rockledge,
New Smyrna Beach, Edgewater, Cocoa, South Daytona, Holly Hill,
Cocoa Beach, Satellite Beach, Cape Canaveral, Oak Hill,
Scottsmoor, Mims, Haulover Canal, Titusville Airport and
Playalinda Beach.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

include up to 1.8 ft of surge that will enhance the astronomical
tide and flooding threat. High tide varies up to 90 minutes
earlier or later along the Pacific Coast and through the San
Francisco Bay, respectively.

particulate levels are expected to be in the Unhealthy for Sensitive

closed as much as possible.

http://www.in.gov/idem/airmonitoring/smogwatch/

livestock have adequate food, unfrozen water, and warmth. Cover or
tend to sensitive crops, plants, and vegetation.

The officials at the Indiana Department of Environmental Management
have declared a Local Air Quality Advisory for Elkhart County, in
effect from 6 PM Saturday November 21st to 10 AM EST Sunday November
22nd.

A Local Air Quality Advisory for PM 2.5 has been issued. Fine
particulate levels are expected to be in the Unhealthy for Sensitive
Groups range. Active children and adults, and people with
respiratory disease, such as asthma should limit prolonged outdoor
exposure.

Due to observed and forecasted high concentration of PM2.5 readings
in the area, recommendations are for the public to reduce or avoid
exertion or heavy work outdoors and keep windows and doors closed as
much as possible.

For additional information, please visit the IDEM Smog page at:

http://www.in.gov/idem/airmonitoring/smogwatch/
